title: Central Maui wastewater reclamation facility funding
summary: On Nov. 10, the commission voted 6-0 to back the Planning Department's land use recommendation for about 14.9 acres for the Central Maui wastewater reclamation facility, sending it to the County Council with comments such as maximizing nitrogen removal. The plant would treat up to 4 million gallons a day, all as R1 recycled water. Officials expect it to run in late 2029 or later, ahead of a school's July 2031 need.

timeline.text: The motion passed with six yes votes.
Comments to be sent to the Council include designing the soil treatment system for maximum nitrogen removal.
Staff will send the Council the commission's recommendation along with commissioners' comments.
A commissioner moved to support the Planning Department's recommendation, which goes to the County Council.
A wastewater official said the new plant would take about 1.5 million of the 5.5 million gallons per day now going to the existing plant.
A second testifier supported the project.
One testifier asked the commission to delay action until several issues are resolved.
The project team said the requests go next to the Maui County Council, then construction permits and construction.
The plant is designed to treat up to 4 million gallons per day.
A soil aquifer treatment system will be the backup disposal system the health department requires.
All treated water is meant to be R1 recycled water, which the engineer called the highest quality.
The project team said the inland site protects against tsunamis, shoreline erosion and sea level rise.
The facility would add treatment capacity and make recycled water for farming and other non-drinking uses.
The county wants land use changes on about 14.9 acres to build a new Central Maui wastewater reclamation facility.
The director confirmed the 14.9-acre plant site does not need the Land Use Commission because it is under 15 acres.
